key_concepts: Atoms are electrically neutral when protons equal electrons
Ions form when atoms lose or gain electrons to achieve noble gas stability
Metals tend to lose valence electrons and form positively charged cations
Nonmetals tend to gain electrons and form negatively charged anions
Sodium loses one electron to become Na+ like neon; chlorine gains one to become Cl- like a
Electron transfer from a metal to a nonmetal creates oppositely charged ions that attract,
The Law of Conservation of Matter requires lost electrons to be gained by another atom
Cations are named with the element name plus 'ion'; anions use the element stem plus '-ide
Ionic compounds such as NaCl, MgO, KCl, and MgCl2 form from cation-anion attraction
Chemical formulas of ionic compounds show the ratio of ions needed to balance charges
